Me or the Machine

I've been recorded 24/7 for 7 weeks. Now an AI can be me.

Jaideep Aher, Duke University, AIPI 590 Responsible AI, fall 2026
It only needed 48 of my sentences.A Bee pendant has recorded nearly everything I have said since 2 October. An AI read 48 lines from it and wrote 47 more in my voice.
My girlfriend scored 50% at telling us apart, on her third try. So would a coin.
Take the test, see the charts
Its AI summaries had picked up my finances and private health information. I never thought of those talks as recorded. It scared me.

After 7 weeks, my pendant holds

Every conversation, word for word
An AI summary of every day
Where I was
Other people's words, without their consent

How the test worked

I took 48 real lines from the pendant, after removing anything private. A language model read them and wrote 47 twin lines. Ten people who know me judged one shuffled line at a time: "really him" or "AI twin". All knew some were fake.

Twin lines passed as often

Sensitivity d′ = -0.06 (0 = cannot tell apart). Friends said "him" 57.5% of the time, which helps an impostor.

49%
of 160 saved judgments were right. A coin flip.
78 of 160, 95% interval 41% to 56%, p = 0.81. Per judge: mean 49%. With three reported 30-line scores: 111 of 250 (44%).
Right (78)Wrong (82)50% mark

Evidence of no skill, not too little data

Could this sample catch real skill?Yes. A true accuracy of 61% would show 80% of the time.
Accuracy within 50% ± 10?Yes. Equivalence test p = 0.015.
Guessing or some ability?Guessing, about 10 times more likely (Bayes factor).
Can a style detector do better?No. 59% on all 95 lines, p = 0.11.

Agreement was below chance (Fleiss' κ = -0.17); their majority vote was right on only 3 of 20.

Next steps

  1. A twin that knows nothing about me. The missing control: does personal data matter at all?
  2. A twin fed all seven weeks. How much do the recordings themselves add to the risk?
  3. Real conversations and a cloned voice, where shared memories should help friends.
  4. Can people learn? The live test now gives instant feedback; those rounds show if accuracy rises.
  5. Test the defence: does a family check question stop a twin?
  6. Audit AI recorders: what each stores, for how long, and who can see it.

Nobody was reliably good

Each dot is one judge. Only one scored above 50% (14 of 20, not significant alone).

Leaks are not hypothetical

2023Amazon, now Bee's owner, paid $25M for keeping kids' Alexa voice recordings after deletion requests.
202323andMe: genetic data of 6.9M people stolen, unnoticed for months.
2025DeepSeek left users' chat logs online with no password.

Leaked pendant data could be used to impersonate you, blackmail you, guess your security answers, find you, and expose everyone you talk to.

Should you wear one? Think hard. If you do:

Assume it leaks one day; mute it for private talk
Delete transcripts often; prefer on-device processing
Strong password, two-factor login, few connected apps
Agree a family check question; never pay because of a text
Limits. Ten judges; three 30-line scores were reported, not saved. Twin lines were written with my real lines in view, the best case for the twin. Real lines keep speech-to-text errors.
Ethics. Judges knew some lines were AI-written; nothing was sent as me. Related work. Turing (1950), Computing Machinery and Intelligence. Jones and Bergen (2025), Large Language Models Pass the Turing Test. Park et al. (2024), Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People.
